messages:
maria: heads-up - running into a bundler/ts interop mess with our JS SDK in the edge sample. Works in node:18 locally but fails when built for Vercel Edge using vite+esbuild with either a type error during build or a runtime: "Cannot use import statement outside a module" when it hits a conditional dynamic import.
aj: can you paste the smallest repro and the exact error output?

maria: minimal repro outline:
- TS module `src/auth.ts` conditionally imports an adapter depending on runtime target (edge vs node)
- adapters export shapes differ: legacy.ts exports `export default function legacyAdapter(){}`; modern.ts exports `export const adapter = () => {}` and `export default adapter` is missing
- build with vite (ssr: true) -> esbuild transforms cause named/default mismatch

Build-time error seen during CI with webpack target:
```
ERROR in ./src/auth.ts
Module parse failed: Unexpected token (12:0)
You may need an appropriate loader to handle this file type, currently no loaders are configured to process this file.
```
Runtime error on Edge build (Vercel):
```
ReferenceError: exports is not defined
    at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap:24)
    at runtime (edge-handler)
```

maria: failing code (simplified):
```ts
// src/auth.ts
export async function chooseAdapter() {
  if (process.env.TARGET === 'legacy') {
    const mod = await import('./adapters/legacy')
    return mod.default
  }
  const mod = await import('./adapters/modern')
  // expect mod.adapter, but sometimes mod comes back as { default: { adapter: fn } }
  return mod.adapter
}
```

liam: this is classic bundler/tscfg shape mismatch. Different bundlers and TS emit options create different interop wrappers. Vite+esbuild can wrap CJS->ESM in dev vs prod differently. Webpack loader chain also changes where default/named end up.
sam: quick workaround for consumers: use a safe resolver helper: `const p = await import(...); const normalized = (p && (p.default || p));` and then pull named exports off normalized. Also add `export { adapter }` alongside `export default adapter` in our shipped adapters to cover both shapes.
aj: SDK-level fix: add tiny util `normalizeModuleImport<T>(m: any): T { return m && (m.__esModule ? m.default : m) }` with types; include in bundle for edge. Also update docs and sample to recommend using the helper for conditional imports.
maria: added note: tsconfig settings that influence this: `esModuleInterop`, `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`, and `module` (esnext vs commonjs). Consumers using `module: commonjs` will see different shapes after bundling. We'll include a matrix in the sample repo.

ci-bot: CI log excerpt: `TypeScript error TS1208: 'Cannot compile namespaces across multiple files'` when mixing `module: commonjs` and `target: es2022` in sampleapp.

sam: for webpack folks add rule: set `module: { rules: [{ test: /\.m?js$/, type: 'javascript/auto' }] }` to avoid webpack converting ESM imports incorrectly. For vite/rollup you can add `build.rollupOptions.external` to avoid bundling that module. But these are advanced knobs.

maria: plan agreed: 1) update our sample adapters to export both default and named exports; 2) add `normalizeModuleImport` helper in SDK and in examples; 3) create `samples/dx-bundler-repros` with tiny apps and configs (vite, rollup, webpack) + tsconfig variants + README with repro steps; 4) add a CI smoke job that runs an esbuild/vite bundle and checks runtime import shapes with a small harness.
aj: I'll open the SDK PR for the helper+types. I'll also add a `CHANGELOG` entry explaining the compatibility shim.

liam: we should also add a unit that uses `esbuild.build({ bundle: true, write: false })` to produce an in-memory bundle and then `vm.runInNewContext` to assert `normalizeModuleImport` works on the output shape. Catches regressions without full deploys.
maria: sounds good. I'll scaffold the sample repo branch and paste the link here when done. Also will include specific minimal webpack config that reproduces the parse error so SREs can reproduce locally.

devx-bot: created ticket RW-768 "bundler import shape mismatch: samples + SDK shim" and assigned to @maria and @aj.

aj: thanks all. If anyone else has seen other weird interop shapes (double-wrapped default, __esModule missing), drop a short note here with exact bundler+tsconfig so we can expand the test matrix.
